task.title: M1: codeviz analyze command producing cached snapshots for Capacitor and workbook
task.description:
Wire everything from milestone 1 into the first user-facing command: codeviz analyze [ref...] (default HEAD). For each ref it resolves the ref, checks the cache, materializes a detached worktree when needed, runs all matching adapters plus the history layer, merges the result into a complete Snapshot with repo identity and toolVersion, and writes it to the cache. WORKTREE is analyzed but never cached. The command prints a short summary (files, functions, languages and tiers, cache path) and supports --since and --json.

Acceptance criteria:
- codeviz analyze with no args analyzes HEAD and writes ~/.cache/codeviz/<repo-id>/<sha>.json.gz; a second run is a cache hit and says so.
- codeviz analyze main v1.0.0 <sha> analyzes several refs, using temporary worktrees that are gone afterwards.
- codeviz analyze WORKTREE prints a summary and leaves no cache file.
- --json emits the full snapshot on stdout; --since forwards to the history layer.
- Running against the Capacitor repo and the workbook repo both complete and produce valid snapshots (schema-checked), and the timings are noted in the PR.
- The bundled Node build (not just bun run) is what is exercised in at least one integration test.
